Compare a quorum of lenses and resolve them into one verdict

Source: R/quorum.R
quorum.Rd

The front door. Each lens is gated on its own declared scope, then asked to fit; a lens that declines either is recorded as having declined and contributes no number. The lenses that returned draws are compared with the agreement semantics, weighed by the independence ledger, and resolved through the declared policy, and the whole comparison is emitted as a manifest the rest of the orchestra can read.

Usage

quorum(
  lenses,
  spec = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  policy,
  grid = NULL,
  decide = NULL,
  data_independence = NA
)

Arguments

lenses

A quorum_lens(), a list of them, or their registered names.

spec

The estimand specification each lens's scope and fit receive.

data

The data each lens's fit receives.

policy

A quorum_policy() declaring the fallback order and quorum.

grid

The candidate grid a decision is taken over, or NULL.

decide

An optional function (draws, grid) returning a list with action, abstained, reason and grounding, supplied by the caller – a decision layer's wrapper, for instance. Without one, a contributing lens is decisive and its action is NA: quorum compares lenses and never prices a decision itself.

data_independence

Single logical: do the lenses read independent upstream data? FALSE blocks the manifest's grounded token, NA records that it was not declared.

Value

A quorum_verdict().

Details

A disagreement between two lenses that cannot express the same response shapes is recorded as a finding rather than counted as discordance: the more expressive lens seeing a plateau the other cannot represent is information about the pair, not evidence that either is wrong.

The status is "no_quorum" when fewer lenses contribute than the policy requires, "not_computed" when there is nothing to compare or the metric layer is unavailable, "concordant" when every counted pair agrees, and "discordant" otherwise. A pair the metric layer could not compare is not concordant, so it makes the status "discordant"; the agreement matrix names it as inconclusive rather than as disagreement.

No quorum means no number. When fewer lenses contribute than the policy requires, the resolution abstains whatever the contributing lenses said, and the verdict carries the typed decline that says so.

See also

quorum_policy(), quorum_resolve(), quorum_manifest().

Examples

fit_fn <- function(spec, data, ...) {
  quorum_draws(list(`(Intercept)` = stats::rnorm(200L)),
               source = "example")
}
one <- quorum_lens("one", "example", fit_fn,
                   c(sampler = "a", objective = "b", priors = "c",
                     data_prep = "d"))
two <- quorum_lens("two", "example", fit_fn,
                   c(sampler = "w", objective = "x", priors = "y",
                     data_prep = "z"))
quorum(list(one, two), policy = quorum_policy(c("one", "two")))
#> <quorum verdict> status: concordant
#>   lenses: 2 (2 contributing, 0 abstained)
#>   carried: one (decide) -> no number issued
#>   findings: 0
#>   independence: Agreement between lenses fitted to the same data is agreement, not corroboration of a shared data fact.
